MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 26, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on June 26, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 21, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  Council Member Bucknum

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation: Significant Exposure to
  Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) or (3) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9

CS2. Conference with legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (1 case)

CS3. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6

City Council Minutes  1  June 26, 2018
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

Mayor Sachs recessed the meeting to Closed Session at 5:02 p.m. The City Council reconvened
at 6:00 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Bucknum was absent).

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session agenda items CS1 and CS2, the
Council received an update and provided direction to staff but no reportable actions occurred. For
item CS3, the City Council gave consideration and provided direction but no reportable action
occurred.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  OCTA Presentation on I-5 Widening Project

  The City Council received the presentation from Niall Barrett, Program Manager with
  Orange County Transportation Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Harry Lenczyk, M.V.: stated that American Golf is proposing to sell the Casta del Sol golf course
but residents want the facilities to continue to be available in the future. He asked the City Council
to help keep the golf course in operation.

Deborah Cunningham-Skurnik, M.V.: announced that the democratic group “Orange County
Students for City Council” will have candidates in several local elections and she introduced
Mahmoud El-Farra, who will be running for Mission Viejo City Council in November, 2018.

Mahmoud El-Farra, M.V.: expressed concern about environmental issues and the drought and
offered ideas for the City of Mission Viejo to do more in these areas.

Tim Lane, M.V.: expressed concern that American Golf is going to sell the Casta del Sol golf
course to a buyer that will change it to something other than a golf course.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed his plight to encourage Orange County cities to implement
reforms at the Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA). He noted that the City of Placentia has
pulled out of OCFA and the City of Irvine is voting this evening whether or not to do the same.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.
City Council Minutes  2  June 26, 2018
 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Bucknum

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of June 12, 2018, as presented.

2.  General Municipal Election - November 6, 2018

  (1) Adopted Resolution 18-21 Calling for the Holding of a General Municipal Election to
  be Held on Tuesday, November 6, 2018, for the Election of Certain Officers as Required
  by the Provisions of the Laws of the State of California Relating to General Law Cities; (2)
  adopted Resolution 18-22 Requesting the Board of Supervisors of the County of Orange
  to Consolidate a General Municipal Election to be Held on November 6, 2018, with the
  Statewide General Election to be Held on the Same Date pursuant to § 10403 of the
  Elections Code; (3) adopted Resolution 18-23 Adopting Regulations for Candidates for
  Elective Officer Pertaining to Candidates Statements Submitted to the Voters at an Election
  to be Held on November 6, 2018; and (4) directed the City Clerk to schedule the adoption
  of the resolution citing the election results and administration of the oath to the newly
  elected Council Members on December 11, 2018, or as soon as possible thereafter.

3.  Check Register Dated June 1, 2018 in the Amount of $494,831.12

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated June 8, 2018 in the Amount of $1,534,444.69

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority Budget - Fiscal Year 2018/19

  Adopted Housing Authority Resolution 18-02 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo
  Housing Authority (MVHA) for 2018/19 Fiscal Year.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority Budget - Fiscal Year
  2018/19

  Adopt CDFA Resolution 18-02 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo Community
  Development Financing Authority for the 2018/19 Fiscal Year.

7.  Establish an Appropriations Limit for the 2018-19 Fiscal Year

  Adopted Resolution 18-24 Establishing an Appropriations Limit for the 2018/19 Fiscal
  Year.
City Council Minutes  3  June 26, 2018
 8.  Agreement for Professional Services for Business Attraction - Buxton

  Approved Agreement with Buxton from July 1, 2018, to June 30, 2021 (three years), for
  an amount not to exceed $150,000 for business attraction services.

9.  2018 Residential Resurfacing (CIP 19838)-Slurry Seal

  Approved the bid specifications, subject to minor revisions required by the City Engineer,
  and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.

10.  Federal-Aid Citywide Systemic Safety Analysis Report Program (SSARP) Project
  (Engineering Services)

  Adopted Resolution 18-25 Approving and Authorizing Execution of Program Supplement
  No. R13 to the Administering Agency-State Master Agreement No. 00402S for Federal-
  Aid Projects between the State Department of Transportation and the City of Mission
  Viejo.

11.  Alicia Parkway & Marguerite Parkway Intersection Improvements (CIP 17232) and
  Santa Margarita Parkway & Marguerite Parkway Intersection Improvements (CIP
  17233)

  Approved the plans and specifications and authorized staff to advertise for bids for the
  Alicia Parkway and Marguerite Parkway (CIP 17232) and Santa Margarita Parkway and
  Marguerite Parkway (CIP 17233) Intersection Improvement Projects.

12.  Renewed Measure M2 Eligibility Submittal to the Orange County Transportation
  Authority

  (1) Adopted Resolution 18-26 Satisfying Renewed Measure M2 Eligibility Requirements
  for Fiscal Year 2018/19, Concerning the Status and Update of the City of Mission Viejo
  2018 Pavement Management Program Update and Adopting a Seven-Year Public Works
  Capital Improvement Program Beginning with the 2018/19 Fiscal Year; and, (2) directed
  staff to transmit said resolution and reports to the Orange County Transportation Authority
  by June 29, 2018, to maintain the City's continued eligibility in receiving Fiscal Year
  2018/19 Renewed Measure M2 local fair-share revenues and in pursuing competitive grant
  funding opportunities.

13.  Public Works Professional Services Consultant Team

  (1) Authorized staff to add ENGEO Incorporated to the Professional Services Consultant
  Team roster; and (2) authorized the City Manager to execute new contracts for the period
  July 1, 2018, through June 30, 2020, with members of the Professional Services Consultant
  Team on an as-needed basis.

14.  2018 Residential Resurfacing-Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 19838)-
  Contract
City Council Minutes  4  June 26, 2018
   Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to All American Asphalt in the
  amount of $1,667,667.00.

15.  Replacement Starting Blocks - Marguerite Aquatics Complex

  Ratified purchase of replacement starting blocks in the amount of $57,307.51.

16.  Cordova Park Play Area Renovations (CIP 306) - Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty-five (35) days respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City; and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of $34,279.55
  thirty-five (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

17.  Annual Routine Street Sweeping Services

  Approved the Fourth Amendment with Sunset Property Services for the period of July 1,
  2018, through June 30, 2019, in the amount of $370,179.43.

18.  Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvements, Shops Boulevard to Center Drive
  - CIP 18239

  (1) Awarded the construction contract to Horizons Construction Company International,
  Inc. for the Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvements, Shops Boulevard to Center
  Drive - (CIP 18239), in an amount not to exceed $634,640 and (2) adopted Resolution 18-
  27 Amending the Fiscal Year 2017-2018 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement
  Project 18239.

19.  Replacing Core Engines of Redundant Network Switches at City Hall

  Approved entering into agreement for professional services and issuance of purchase order
  for network hardware to Resilient Communications in the amount of $80,695.23 including
  a 10% contingency.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

NEW BUSINESS

23.  Small Park Infill Projects and Park Security Fencing

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  5  June 26, 2018
   The following expressed concern with proposed park infill improvements for various
  reasons such as neighborhood congestion, increased noise and safety matters: Brian
  Schneider, M.V.; Kyle Jones, M.V.; Matt Brown, M.V.; Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.; Mike
  Jones, M.V.; Eric Burgdorf, M.V.; Donna Oblea, M.V.; Dave Gove, M.V.; H. Charton,
  M.V.; and Cathy Schlicht, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to reject
  the whole plan with the exception of the safety fencing at Hankey School and direct staff
  to keep discussions open for the proposed community garden on school district property.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  Sachs
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

  Note: Later in the meeting, Mayor Sachs requested that the matter be reconsidered as he
  inadvertently voted no and wished to register a yes vote.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to
  reconsider agenda item 23.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to reject
  the whole plan with the exception of the safety fencing at Hankey School and direct staff
  to keep discussions open for the proposed community garden on school district property.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

OLD BUSINESS

20.  City Operating and Capital Improvement Program Revised Budget - Fiscal Year
  2018/19

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report and outlined
  various revisions to the report and resolutions that were made subsequent to publication of
  the agenda:

City Council Minutes  6  June 26, 2018
   1. For State Gas Tax Fund revenues, the proposed revenue should be $2,116,460, not
  $2,116,370.
  2. For SB1 revenues, the proposed revenue should be $1,618,286, not $11,618,286.
  3. Under the fiscal impact summary, the State Gas Tax Fund revenue amendment
  should be $(1,675,895), not $(1,331,190) and the new increase/(decrease) in fund
  balance for this same fund should be $(695,693), not $(350,988).
  4. For the budget resolution, rental fee rates were incorporated into Section 3 and
  Section 11 was modified to appropriate resources directly from the Crown Valley
  Corridor Fee Fund.
  5. For the salary and authorized position schedule resolution, the exhibit references
  were updated to reflect the reference letters on the actual exhibits that are part of
  the resolution.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 18-28 Adopting a Revised Budget for the City of Mission Viejo For FY 2018-
  19 and Appropriating Funds for Fiscal Year 2018-19; and (2) adopt Resolution 18-29
  Amending the City’s Salary Schedule and Authorized Position Schedule Effective July 1,
  2018.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

STAFF REPORTS

26.  FY 2018-19 Law Enforcement Services Agreement and Additional Special
  Enforcement Services Provided by Orange County Sheriff’s Department

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1)
  approve the FY 2018-19 Law Enforcement Services Agreement with the County of Orange
  (A18-16) for an amount not to exceed $19,413,700; and (2) authorize the City Manager to
  approve reimbursements related to special enforcement services in an amount not to exceed
  $35,000 for FY 2018-19.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

City Council Minutes  7  June 26, 2018
 OLD BUSINESS (Continued)

21.  Retiree Healthcare Actuarial Study as of June 30, 2017

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to direct staff to
  deposit monies currently budgeted for the retiree healthcare plan ($221,000) into the
  Section 115 pension trust.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

22. Marguerite Aquatics Complex Renovation CIP 14325- Project Closeout

  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services, presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) approve
  the Seventh Amendment to Construct 1 One Corp in an amount not to exceed $6,229.91 for
  unknown field conditions and site modifications; (2) approve the Second Amendment to
  Griffin Structures in an amount not to exceed $10,000 for additional Construction
  Management Services; (3) adopt Resolution 18-30 Amending CIP 14325 Marguerites
  Aquatics Complex Budget by $13,000; (4) certify the completion of and accept the
  improvements for the subject project; (5) authorize the City Manager to sign the Notice of
  Completion; (6) authorize the City Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County
  of Orange and to release the Faithful Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty-
  Five Days (35) days respectively, after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion
  contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City and; (7) authorize the payment
  of the final retention of $923,503.18 thirty-five (35) days after of recordation of the Notice
  of Completion.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

24.  Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Sachs presented the report.

City Council Minutes  8  June 26, 2018
 25.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  The report was deferred to a future meeting.

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

27.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update from Chief Capobianco

  Chief Capobianco discussed OCFA’s Wildland Resource Defense Planner who provides
  live fuel moisture measurements that are utilized to evaluate danger areas in fire season.
  He also discussed OCFA's participation in Water Safety Day at Montanoso Recreation
  Center, the final 2017 drowning statistics, Truck 9's rope rescue training, and fireworks
  safety. Chief Capobianco concluded his report with condolences to the family and co-
  workers of Captain Dave Rosa who was killed as the result of an ambush while responding
  to a call in the City of Long Beach.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

28.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum was absent.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell expressed his sadness at the news of Captain Dave Rosa’s death. He
announced that the Nadadores 50-year reunion was held last weekend and it was a wonderful
celebration. Council Member Goodell shared that everyone in attendance was very impressed with
the improvements to the Marguerite Aquatics Center.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley stated that everyone’s hearts go out to the fallen firefighter’s family. She
said it is such a reminder that public safety officers get up every day, go to work and they don't
know if they'll come back. She noted that she has been praying for Captain Rosa’s family and will
continue to do so. Council Member Kelley reminded residents that the 4th of July Street Faire will
be held from noon to 9:00 p.m. on Olympiad Road between Marguerite and Melinda. She
expressed her appreciation to the Mission Viejo Activities Committee who put the event on every
year. She said there are just a few people doing a ton of work for the benefit of thousands of people.
Council Member Kelley reminded residents of the Boots, Beer & Barbecue event, a fundraiser to
benefit the City’s adopted Marines. It will be held on Sunday, July 22 from 4:00 to 7:00 p.m.
Tickets are $25 per person and can be purchased at Norman P. Murray Community Center.
City Council Minutes  9  June 26, 2018
 Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that the Orange County Registrar of Voters has certified the
June election results and he congratulated all those who won and those who ran for public office.
He said he looks forward to the July 4th street faire and fireworks and he announced that singer
LeAnn Rimes will perform at Lake Mission Viejo on July 7, 2018.

Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs discussed Consent Calendar item 16 and noted that the Cordova Park play area
improvement project was under budget and he said that is something to be proud of. He also
commended staff for looking at consolidating street sweeping services with other cities to try and
reduce the annual cost of street sweeping (item 17). Referencing agenda item 19, Mayor Sachs
discussed a recent Wall Street Journal article which reported that there has been a 38% increase in
municipalities being hit with ransomware and other disruptions. He said he found it interesting
that the City has policies and procedures in place to deal with ransomware but the FBI is
encouraging cities not to pay the ransom if they are hit. He asked if the City has cyber security
insurance and City Manager Wilberg confirmed that it does. Mayor Sachs announced that the City
of Placentia has voted, but not yet notified the Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA,) that they
will be pulling out of OCFA in two years. He said the reason they are leaving is that they cannot
afford any more services. The City of Seal Beach looked at doing the same but found that staying
with OCFA was considerably cheaper than having the City of Long Beach provide fire services
for them. Mayor Sachs noted that the City of Irvine, on a 3-1 vote, will also be leaving the OCFA.
In closing, he asked if he can change his vote for item 23 because he misinterpreted the motion for
the park infills and he voted no because he doesn’t want to do the projects. City Attorney Curley
recommended that the Council first vote to reconsider the item and then take a new vote for item
23 (see page 6).

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:53 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, July 10, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of July 10, 2018

City Council Minutes  10  June 26, 2018
